title: Śrī Śikṣāṣṭakam
author: by Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu in Sanskrit
subtitle: Verse Eight

translation: “Kṛṣṇa may embrace me in love or trample me under His feet. He may break my heart by hiding Himself from me. Let that debauchee do whatever He likes, but He will always be the only Lord of my life.”
*Corresponding Bengali composition by Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur:*
O my friends! Listen to my words. I am filled to overflowing with devotional ecstasy when I have a divine vision of that thief who has stolen my heart.
And when I want to see Him more clearly, He disappears from sight and becomes invisible. Again, not seeing Him, my soul weeps and my grief knows no bounds.

text: jagatera bandhu sei kabhu more laya sātha
yathā tathā rākhu more āmāra se prāṇanātha
translation: Sometimes Kṛṣṇa, the friend of the universe, takes me as one of His own, and sometimes He ignores me, but however He keeps me, He is the only Lord of my life.

text: punaḥ adarśana diyā    dagdha kare mora hiyā
translation: When He gives His blissful audience to me, He gives happiness to my soul. He gives me great ecstasy by allowing me to see Him and by speaking affectionately to me. Again He goes away, removing Himself from my sight. And by not letting me see Him, He burns my heart with the fire of separation.

text: yāhe tāra sukha haya, sei sukha mama
nija sukhe duḥkhe mora sarvadāi sama
translation: But even though He pains my soul in this way, He is still the Lord of my life. Whatever is His happiness is also my happiness. And so, for me, my own happiness and distress is all the same.

In this way, Bhakti Vinod, in both union and separation, knows that Kṛṣṇa is the only Lord of his soul. Kṛṣṇa’s happiness is my happiness. He is the Lord of my life; there is no other Lord for me than Him.
